item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 091738
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Wed Sep 9 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lowell, located several hundred miles north-northwest of the
Hawaiian Islands.

Central Portion and West Portion of the East Pacific (EP96):
Showers and thunderstorms continue to show signs of organization
with an area of low pressure located several hundred miles
south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
peninsula. Environmental conditions are expected to support
continued development of this system, and a tropical depression is
expected to form later today or tonight. as the system moves
generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph. For more information,
including gale warnings, please see High Seas Forecast issued by
National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Portion and West Portion of the East Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form several hundred miles
south of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula this
weekend or early next week. Some gradual development is possible
thereafter, and a tropical depression could form early next week
while the system moves generally west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

Well South-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form several hundred miles
south-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands. Some gradual development is
possible late this week into this weekend as this system moves
slowly north-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Evans/Kelly

item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Wed Sep 09 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 092038
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fourteen-E Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
200 PM PDT Wed Sep 09 2026
 
...TROPICAL DEPRESSION FORMS WELL SOUTH-SOUTHWEST OF THE BAJA
CALIFORNIA PENINSULA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 115.2W
ABOUT 605 MI...975 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Fourteen-E was located near latitude 15.7 North, longitude 115.2
West. The depression is moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph
(15 km/h), and a generally westward motion is expected over the 
next couple of days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual strengthening is forecast over the next several days, and 
the depression could become a tropical storm tonight or Thursday.  
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Fourteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Wed Sep 09 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 092039
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Fourteen-E Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
200 PM PDT Wed Sep 09 2026

Satellite imagery indicates that an area of low pressure (Invest 
EP96) has developed a more organized circulation, along with 
persistent convection east of its center. Scatterometry data from 
around 1700 UTC revealed a slightly elongated but closed circulation 
with a max wind of around 30 kt. Subjective Dvorak analysis from 
TAFB rated this system at 2.5/2.5, or an intensity at around 35 kt. 
Given the scatterometry data and satellite imagery, advisories have 
been initiated on Tropical Depression 14-E, with an initial 
intensity of 30 kt.

The initial motion of this system was estimated at 285/8 kt, but 
this is uncertain since the system has only recently formed. Global 
models depict mid-level ridging building north of the depression, 
so a primarily west to west-northwest motion is expected over the 
next several days. By late this weekend into early next week, the
guidance depicts a slight weakening in the ridge to the north that 
will shift the track slightly more west-northwestward, before the 
ridge amplifies once again and pushes the system 
west-southwestward.  The official track forecast reflects a blend of 
the HCCA and GDMI, which is on the southern side of the guidance 
envelope. 

The depression is expected to enter an environment favorable for 
gradual strengthening. The SHIPS guidance depicts low vertical wind 
shear, as well as ample mid-level moisture and favorable SSTs, which 
should allow the depression to strengthen to a tropical storm 
tonight or Thursday and into a hurricane later this weekend. The 
official intensity forecast reflects a slower strengthening trend 
within the first couple of days, given that scatterometry data still 
depicts a depression with a slightly elongated center. By the end of 
the week, however, steady strengthening is forecast, and the NHC 
prediction lies on the higher end of the guidance envelope given the 
favorable environment ahead of the depression.
